How can I change a ceramic product photo to a three-quarter view while preserving its shape and material? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
Changing a flat or front-facing product photo of a ceramic item into a three-quarter view while preserving its distinct shape and material properties requires either advanced AI manipulation, precision 3D warping, or a physical reshoot. Ceramic materials present unique challenges because their glossy glazes, intricate contours, and interior cavities reflect light dynamically. 
magiceraser.live
 +1
Here are the most effective methods to achieve a three-quarter perspective digitally or through photography:
1. Generative AI and View Synthesis Tools
Modern e-commerce AI tools utilize image-to-image and view-synthesis models to rotate a product while maintaining its structural identity.
AI Product Generators: Software explicitly designed for e-commerce allows you to upload an existing image and input a prompt to alter the perspective. For instance, you can use a command like "Three-quarter view of the ceramic item, maintaining exact material, texture, and shape". 
YouTube
·DolphyAI
Consistent Product Replacement: Some workflows allow you to take an inspirational lifestyle image already framed at a three-quarter angle and swap in your product using a strict consistency prompt. 
Instagram
·Safwaan Mujawar
AI Enhancements: If the AI model struggles to properly illuminate the newly exposed inner surfaces or glazes of a ceramic vessel (like a bowl or vase), you can use specialized tools like Magic Eraser's AI Enhance to recover blown-out highlights, brighten dark voids, and balance the dynamic range. 
magiceraser.live
2. Manual 3D Perspective Warping
If you want to manually adjust the angle of the current photo without letting AI hallucinate details, professional editing software offers perspective manipulation.
Photoshop Perspective Warp: Rather than using standard distort tools, duplicate your layer and navigate to Edit > Perspective Warp. You build a 3D grid around the ceramic item and shift the points to rotate the object's planes digitally. 
TikTok
·piximperfects
Canva's Transform Image: For basic perspective shifts, applications like the Transform Image App on Canva allow you to upload an image and drag corner handles to simulate a 3D tilt. 
Canva
 +1
Note on Ceramics: Manual warping works best on flat or geometric items. Highly curved ceramics may look stretched, and their specular reflections (shine) will not update to match the new light angle naturally. 
Pottery Log
3. The Gold Standard: Physical Re-Shooting
Because ceramics interact heavily with light, physically moving the camera is often the only way to flawlessly capture the genuine glaze texture and depth. 
Instagram
·Hayley Reed
 +1
Multi-Angle Framing: Use a steady tripod and a neutral backdrop to take multiple shots, explicitly targeting the 45-degree (three-quarter) angle. This seamlessly captures both the exterior profile and the inside details.
360-Degree Interactive Capture: To completely solve perspective issues for the web, place the item on a rotating turntable and take a series of sequential images. You can then stitch them together using a 360-degree JavaScript viewer. 
YouTube
·Making Photos - Ian's Studio / Ian M Butterfield
 +2
To recommend the absolute best workflow for your project, could you tell me:
What software or AI tools do you currently have access to?
Do you have the physical ceramic item on hand to take a new photo, or are you limited only to the single existing photograph?
What is the exact shape of the ceramic product (e.g., a flat plate, a glossy mug, or an intricate vase)?
